module_title: Spherical Mirrors, Lenses, and Total Internal Reflection
introduction: This level covers curved optical devices and the mathematical rules governing them. It also introduces one of the most important optical phenomena: Total Internal Reflection.

core_concepts.title: Concave vs. Convex Mirrors
core_concepts.description:
1. Concave Mirror (Converging): Reflecting surface is curved inward. Used where magnified images or focused light is needed. (Uses: Dentist's mirror, shaving mirror, vehicle headlights, solar furnaces). 
2. Convex Mirror (Diverging): Reflecting surface is curved outward. It always forms a virtual, erect, and 'diminished' (small) image. (Uses: Rearview mirrors in vehicles because it provides a wider field of view).

core_concepts.title: Lenses and Power
core_concepts.description:
1. Convex Lens: Thicker in the middle, converging. Forms real/inverted images (mostly). 
2. Concave Lens: Thinner in the middle, diverging. Forms virtual/erect/smaller images. 
Power of a Lens ($P$): The reciprocal of focal length ($f$ in meters). $P = 1/f$. 
SI Unit: Diopter (D). Convex has +ve power, Concave has -ve power.

core_concepts.title: Total Internal Reflection (TIR)
core_concepts.description: When light travels from a denser medium to a rarer medium and the angle of incidence is greater than the 'Critical Angle', the light is completely reflected BACK into the denser medium. No refraction occurs.

core_concepts.title: Applications of TIR
core_concepts.description:
Examiners love these: 
1. Sparkling of diamonds. 
2. Mirages in deserts (optical illusion of water). 
3. Optical Fibers (used in telecommunications and endoscopy).

important_entities.name: Optical Fibers
important_entities.significance: Invented by Narinder Singh Kapany. Optical fibers use TIR to transmit light signals over massive distances with almost zero loss of energy.

trap_alerts_and_exceptions.explanation:
Exam Trap: Students often swap the plus and minus signs. 
Mirror Formula: $\frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{v} + \frac{1}{u}$ 
Lens Formula: $\frac{1}{f} = \frac{1}{v} - \frac{1}{u}$ 
(Where $v$ is image distance, $u$ is object distance).

mnemonics_and_tricks.explanation: Vex matches with Vehicles. Remember that convex mirrors are used for rearview because they show a wide area.

exam_strategy_tips: State PCS Exams frequently ask: 'What is the working principle of an Endoscope?' Answer: Total Internal Reflection.
